title.en: To Await Later Ages: From the Grand Historian's Afterword

edition.en: Extracts from the afterword that closes the Shiji (chapter 130), as given on Chinese Wikisource; checked against the version in Sima Qian's biography in the Han shu (chapter 62), which differs only in small words. The omitted passage is marked with a section break.
edition.zh: 节选自《史记》卷一百三十《太史公自序》，据维基文库；并与《汉书·司马迁传》（卷六十二）所录本对校，两本只有虚字等细小差异。删节处以分隔符标出。

basis.en: Completed about 91 BCE; the author died about 86 BCE.
basis.zh: 约成书于公元前 91 年，作者约卒于公元前 86 年。

note.en: In the last chapter of his Records, Sima Qian tells how the work came to him: his father, the court astronomer Sima Tan, took his hand and charged him not to forget what he had meant to write, and he promised to leave nothing out. The closing paragraph says what became of it: a hundred and thirty chapters, 526,500 characters, one copy stored in a famous mountain and another kept in the capital, to await the sages and gentlemen of later ages. Read it beside the letter to Ren An, which describes the same plan from the other side.
note.zh: 在《史记》的最后一篇里，司马迁讲述这部书怎样落到他身上：父亲太史令司马谈拉着他的手，嘱咐他不要忘记自己想写的东西，他答应一点也不遗漏。最后一段交代了书的去处：一百三十篇，五十二万六千五百字，正本藏于名山，副本留在京师，“俟后世圣人君子”。可以和《报任安书》对读，那封信从另一面讲了同一个计划。

excerpt.orig: 藏之名山，副在京師，俟後世聖人君子。
excerpt.en: It is to be stored in a famous mountain, with a copy in the capital, to await the sages and gentlemen of later ages.
excerpt.zh: 藏之名山，副在京师，俟后世圣人君子。

gloss.en: The Feng sacrifice to Heaven on Mount Tai, performed by Emperor Wu in 110 BCE, the first under the Han.
gloss.zh: 指汉武帝于公元前 110 年在泰山举行的封禅，是汉朝第一次封禅。

gloss.en: The Grand Historian: here Sima Tan (d. 110 BCE), Sima Qian's father; later in the chapter, Sima Qian himself.
gloss.zh: 这里指司马迁的父亲司马谈（卒于前 110 年）；后文的“太史公”则是司马迁自称。

gloss.en: The region around Luoyang, where Sima Tan was detained by illness.
gloss.zh: 指洛阳一带，司马谈因病滞留于此。

gloss.en: To have charge of the affairs of heaven: astronomy, the calendar and omens, the historian's first duty.
gloss.zh: 掌管天文、历法、星象之事，这是史官的本职。

gloss.en: The ways of the Dukes of Zhou and Shao, remembered in the 'Zhou nan' and 'Shao nan' sections of the Book of Songs.
gloss.zh: 周公、召公的风化，《诗经》有《周南》《召南》。

gloss.en: The Great King (Gugong Danfu) and his son Wang Ji, grandfather and father of King Wen of Zhou.
gloss.zh: 太王即古公亶父，王季是他的儿子，二人是周文王的祖父和父亲。

gloss.en: Gong Liu and Hou Ji, the earliest ancestors of the Zhou people; Hou Ji was honoured as the god of grain.
gloss.zh: 公刘和后稷是周人更早的祖先；后稷被尊为农神。

gloss.en: Kings You and Li of Western Zhou, remembered as the rulers under whom the dynasty decayed.
gloss.zh: 西周的幽王、厉王，被视为使周室衰败的君主。

gloss.en: The capture of a qilin in 481 BCE, the event with which the Spring and Autumn Annals end.
gloss.zh: 公元前 481 年鲁国猎获麒麟，《春秋》记事止于此。

gloss.en: 紬 (chōu), to draw out and put in order; 史記 here means historical records in general; the stone chambers and metal caskets are the imperial archives.
gloss.zh: 紬，缀集整理；史记，泛指史书；石室金匮，国家藏书和档案之所。

gloss.en: 104 BCE, the year the Taichu calendar was adopted; Sima Qian was among those who drew it up.
gloss.zh: 公元前 104 年，这一年颁行太初历，司马迁参与了制定。

gloss.at: 自周公卒五百歲而有孔子
gloss.at_hans: 自周公卒五百岁而有孔子
gloss.en: After Mencius's saying that a true king, or a sage, appears every five hundred years.
gloss.zh: 本于孟子“五百年必有王者兴”之说。

gloss.en: 讓, to decline modestly. He takes up the five-hundred-year task as his own.
gloss.zh: 让，推辞。他把这五百年的使命当作自己的事。

gloss.en: The burning of the books under Qin in 213 BCE.
gloss.zh: 指公元前 213 年秦朝焚书。

gloss.en: Master Gai, a teacher of the Huang-Lao learning attributed to the Yellow Emperor and Laozi, which guided early Han government.
gloss.zh: 盖公，传授黄老之学（托名黄帝、老子的学说），汉初政治多受其影响。

gloss.en: Shen Buhai and Lord Shang (Shang Yang), thinkers of the school of law.
gloss.zh: 申不害、商鞅，法家人物。

gloss.en: From Laozi, chapter 11: thirty spokes share one hub. Here the image is of ministers gathered around the ruler.
gloss.zh: 语出《老子》第十一章。这里比喻群臣环绕君主。

gloss.en: 526,500 characters, a count the author gives himself; the earlier chapters list the contents, and this sentence gives the size.
gloss.zh: 这是作者自己给出的字数；前面列出篇目，这一句交代全书的规模。

gloss.en: A second copy kept in the capital: the master copy stored away, the duplicate where readers could reach it.
gloss.zh: 副本留在京城：正本收藏起来，副本放在读者够得着的地方。

gloss.en: The afterword is itself the seventieth and last of the Biographies.
gloss.zh: 《自序》本身就是七十列传的第七十篇，也是最后一篇。
